newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria oil joint ventures agree to pay monitors.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria oil joint ventures agree to pay monitors.

text.p: Nigerian joint venture oil producing companies have agreed to pay monitors to inspect crude terminals to ensure that no fraud is taking place, industry officials said on Tuesday.
"Finally we have no choice but to pick up the bill," one official said.

The companies initially opposed the appointment of foreign inspection companies after government accusations that Nigeria was losing 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude to "topping" -- loading more crude into vessels than was originally stated.

"Every barrel is documented and accounted for," Jim Massey, managing director of Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited, said in a recently released video, produced by the companies to counter the accusations.
Nigeria pumps around two million bpd.
The biggest joint venture partners with state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) are Shell, Chevron, Mobil, Elf Aquitaine and Agip.
